findings.finding: Medistim disclosed MNOK 7.5 of paid US tariffs 'deemed unlawful' (IEEPA) with refunds being pursued as of 20 Aug; CBP's refund process (60-90 days from acceptance, ~$100bn refunded by early Aug) makes Q3 receipt/recognition plausible, which would add up to ~MNOK 7.5 to EBIT (~15% of a ~50 MNOK bar) as a one-off.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Medistim one-off of this kind; Q2 2026 (which flagged the refund and tariff cost of MNOK 5) rose +5.58% on the results day.
findings.why_not_priced: The one analyst's EPS (2.09) implies PBT ~50 MNOK, consistent with a normal-quarter build with no refund in it; if a refund were expected the estimate would have stepped up rather than drifted from 2.13 to 2.09 in the last week. Timing of receipt is unconfirmed, and a refund-made beat is typically looked through, so small.
findings.independence: CBP refund pace from a different source: https://taxprofblog.aals.org/2026/04/21/ieepa-tariff-refund-process-begins/ (process opened 20 Apr 2026, 60-90 day refunds).

findings.finding: NOK strengthened through Q3 2026 (USD/NOK 9.909 -> 9.624, -2.9%; EUR/NOK 11.309 -> 10.901, -3.6%), and Medistim's net finance is 'realized and unrealized gains or losses related to currency, cash in USD and EUR, and customer receivables' -- in Q1 2026, with a similar NOK move, net finance was about -5.6 MNOK; a few MNOK loss would trim ~0.1-0.2 NOK off the 2.09 EPS bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (net finance about -5.6 MNOK, EBIT down) was reported on an ex-dividend day; the results-day move reads 0.0 on adjusted closes, so no clean read.
findings.why_not_priced: Below EBIT and usually modelled at zero by a single covering analyst; the market reads Medistim on revenue and EBIT, so even if it lands it is mostly looked through -- hence a fraction of the money.
findings.independence: Company's own description of the net-finance drivers and the Q1/Q2 2026 figures: https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=680454 (Q2 2026 report, net finance +3.6 Q2, -1.9 H1).

findings.finding: Q3 2026 laps hard comps on the company's own numbers: US price increases were 'introduced this quarter' in Q3 2025 (so the ~27pp price contribution to H1 2026 US growth fades), APAC laps +193% (25.2 vs 8.6 MNOK) while Japan transitions to direct sales (-37% in H1), and NOK translation is -5.8% USD / -7.3% EUR YoY on quarter averages; against that EMEA laps -11.8% (direct ops -26.8%). Net, my build lands at ~182 MNOK vs the 186 bar -- a slight downside lean on revenue growth after a +13% run-up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue-led results days have been bought: Q3 2025 +3.17%, Q4 2025 +6.54%, Q2 2026 +5.58%, Q2 2025 +13.91%, Q1 2025 +16.02%; last clear negative was Q1 2024 -4.40%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the comps are in the company's own reports and the single analyst's 186 MNOK (+11.5%) already implies deceleration from Q2's +19.5%. What may not be priced is the stock's run-up (+12.85% in 20 days, +24% in 60) into a quarter whose headline growth mechanically slows; if the market had priced the slowdown the stock would not have rallied into the print on the dividend authorisation alone.

findings.finding: The EGM on 5 Oct 2026 approved (all votes in favour) the board's authorisation to pay quarterly dividends, and the stock rose from 250 to 281 NOK in the following week (+5% on 6 Oct on ~90k shares, about 9x the usual volume); the first quarterly declaration, likely with Q3, is therefore largely in the price and the residual risk is a token amount or deferral to Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Dividend proposals have come with Q4/AGM; no quarterly-dividend history. The authorisation itself moved the stock about +12% over 5 sessions.
findings.why_not_priced: It mostly is: the tape after the EGM shows the market positioned for a quarterly payout. What is not known is the amount and timing; the 2025 dividend (NOK 8.00, 146 MNOK) was already paid in May and Q2 cash was 100.2 MNOK, which limits how large a first quarterly payment can be.
